failure_modes.description: The assumption that elastic deformation reduces effective contact area without increasing turbulence is unsupported and likely false
failure_modes.evidence: Fluid dynamics research shows that surface deformation typically creates additional turbulence and vortices, increasing drag rather than reducing it

failure_modes.description: Contradicts established boundary layer theory where surface compliance often increases drag
failure_modes.evidence: Numerous studies show that compliant surfaces generally increase drag due to energy dissipation and boundary layer disruption

failure_modes.description: The hypothesis breaks at high Reynolds numbers where elastic deformation cannot occur quickly enough
failure_modes.evidence: At high flow rates, the time constant for elastic deformation exceeds the characteristic time of flow disturbances

failure_modes.description: Similar concepts have been thoroughly investigated and shown ineffective decades ago
failure_modes.evidence: 1960s-1980s research on 'dolphin skin' and compliant surfaces showed no net drag reduction

failure_modes.description: The hypothesis directly contradicts its own proposed falsifier
failure_modes.evidence: If drag reduction occurs without deformation, it invalidates the core mechanism, yet the hypothesis claims this as its primary mechanism

failure_modes.description: The mechanism is incompatible with the target application of drag reduction
failure_modes.evidence: Elastic recovery requires energy that would negate any drag reduction benefits
